episode_row: EOD clean exit → Restart=always relaunch loop (NRestarts 0→7 in 25 min)

commits.subject: fix(scheduler): sleep until next-day wakeup after IDLE_END_OF_DAY
commits.body:
Bug: run_day writes IDLE_END_OF_DAY heartbeat then returns. Process exits.
systemd Restart=always re-launches within 30s. New run_day runs through
its full logic, but all post-lock branches short-circuit (pick locked,
games final, result already polled), reaching IDLE_END_OF_DAY again in
~3 min. Observed live 2026-04-23 post-games: NRestarts grew from 0 → 7
in 25 min after both picks' games ended.

Not caught by watchdog kill this time — these are clean process exits,
not SIGABRT. Yesterday's WatchdogSec hardening prevents the silent
SIGABRT cycle but doesn't address the legitimate-clean-exit-into-
restart cycle.

Fix: new _idle_until_next_wakeup(next_wakeup_iso, heartbeat_path) helper
keeps the process alive past IDLE_END_OF_DAY by sleeping (via already-
tested _watchdog_ping_sleep) until state.next_wakeup. Writes SLEEPING
state + sleeping_until metadata so check_heartbeat.py recognizes the
intentional sleep.

3 defensive tests: None wake-time, past wake-time, malformed ISO all
short-circuit to no-op. Future wake-time would require real sleep —
trusts _watchdog_ping_sleep's existing tests.

Full suite: 566 passed (was 563).
